sections.content: No obstante (nevertheless, notwithstanding) is a more formal, written-register alternative to sin embargo -- common in historical and academic prose. It can open a sentence as a connector, or, less commonly, work like a preposition before a noun phrase (no obstante los intentos de...). These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Estas políticas económicas generaron, no obstante, un fuerte endeudamiento externo y una desindustrialización considerable.
items.english: These economic policies nevertheless generated heavy external debt and considerable deindustrialization.

items.spanish: No obstante los intentos de mantenerse en el poder, la junta militar se vio obligada a convocar elecciones.
items.english: Notwithstanding its attempts to remain in power, the military junta was forced to call elections.

items.spanish: El régimen había prometido modernizar la economía; no obstante, los resultados finales estuvieron bastante alejados de esa promesa.
items.english: The regime had promised to modernize the economy; nevertheless, the final results were quite far from that promise.

items.spanish: La guerra fue breve; no obstante, sus consecuencias políticas resultarían decisivas para el futuro inmediato del país.
items.english: The war was brief; nevertheless, its political consequences would prove decisive for the country's immediate future.

sections.content: As a connector between two clauses, no obstante usually sits between commas or starts a new sentence, just like sin embargo. Used before a noun (no obstante + noun), it means despite -- a more formal equivalent of a pesar de.
